Detect compositional outliers

Source: R/comp_outliers.R
comp_outliers.Rd

Flags observations whose ratios between parts are atypical, using the robust Mahalanobis distance of Filzmoser and Hron (2008) computed in pivot isometric log-ratio coordinates. An observation is an outlier when its distance exceeds sqrt(qchisq(quantile, df = D - 1)) for a D-part composition. The distance is invariant to the closure of the composition and to the choice of ILR pivot.

Usage

comp_outliers(data, parts, quantile = 0.975, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the composition parts, free of zeroes.

parts

Character vector of column names making up the composition (at least two parts).

quantile

Chi-squared probability setting the outlier cutoff. Defaults to 0.975.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to robCompositions::outCoDa(). The useful one is alpha, the proportion of observations MCD retains in its subset search (default 0.5, the most robust; higher values trade robustness for efficiency). The coda argument of outCoDa() cannot be overridden, and passing it is an error.

Value

A tibble with one row per observation and the columns .row (position in data), distance (robust Mahalanobis distance in ILR coordinates), limit (the cutoff, constant down the column), and is_outlier (logical, distance > limit). Rows are never removed; acting on the flags is left to the caller.

Details

The centre and covariance come from the minimum covariance determinant (MCD) estimator, which resists the outliers it is meant to find. Its classical counterpart, the arithmetic mean and sample covariance, is itself distorted by them (the masking effect) and is not offered.

MCD estimates the covariance from a randomized subset search, so distances vary slightly between calls. A call to set.seed() beforehand makes the flags reproducible.

Detection requires a zero-free composition. Zeroes can be imputed first with comp_impute(), or the composition built with declare_composition(), which imputes before it flags.

References

Filzmoser, P., & Hron, K. (2008). Outlier detection for compositional data using robust methods. Mathematical Geosciences, 40, 233-248. doi:10.1007/s11004-007-9141-5

Rousseeuw, P.J., & Van Driessen, K. (1999). A fast algorithm for the minimum covariance determinant estimator. Technometrics, 41, 212-223. doi:10.1080/00401706.1999.10485670

See also

declare_composition(), which calls this when detect_outliers = TRUE; comp_impute() to remove zeroes first.

Other declare and describe composition: comp_impute(), declare_composition(), plot.compD(), summary.compD()

Examples

set.seed(1)
out <- comp_outliers(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"))
sum(out$is_outlier)
#> [1] 14
